id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979) and held professorships at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007) and Ochanomizu University (~2007–2018).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Mipham Chokyi Lodro worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973), and later taught Trinley Thaye Dorje and Ole Nydahl.

Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1994) as her doctoral supervisor, Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest under Nae Ionescu, studied at the University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, and held professorships at Bucharest, the Sorbonne, and Chicago.
Mireille Helffer was a Tibetologist and scholar who served as Chargé de Recherche at the CNRS (~1969–1993) and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Otago (MA) and University of Calgary (PhD, 2005) under John A. Baker, and held posts at the University of New South Wales and University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Zagreb, Hague Academy of International Law, International Faculty of Comparative Law, and University of Ljubljana (PhD, 1960). He held faculty posts at Zagreb, Pennsylvania, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Yale.

Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Mysore and Pune under Madhukar Narhar Deshpande. He worked at Karnatak University and the Karnataka archaeology department, and served as Director General of the ASI (1984–1987).
Mitchell G. Weiss works in Indology. He studied under Ludo Rocher and has served as a professor at the University of Basel.

Mitsuji Fukunaga worked in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University, and held professorships at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945) and held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1986–1989).
Mitsunobu Nakasone works in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo, Munich (PhD), and Kokugakuin (PhD), he held professorships at Tsukuba and Nihon University, and directed the Eastern Institute (~1999–2010).

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1958–1976) and at International Buddhist University (attested 1976).

Mizuho Okita works in Indology and religious studies. She earned a BA from Tokai University, studied at Gakushuin University under Katsuhiko Kamimura and Atsuhiko Yoshida, and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (~2008).
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Tokai University (attested 1976 and 1987).
